lead: A B-spline is a curve built from control points and a knot vector. Unlike a Bezier curve, each control point influences only a short span, so moving one point changes a small piece of the shape. The knot vector sets where the curve starts, ends and joins. This local control is why B-splines and their rational form NURBS are used in CAD, font outlines, car body design and animation paths.
prereq: You need: Chapter 3.4 for control points, blending and the Bezier special case, and Unit 2 for matrix forms.

blocks.text: A B-spline of degree p has control points P₀, P₁, …, Pₙ and a knot vector U = (u₀, u₁, …, uₘ). The knots are non-decreasing: u₀ ≤ u₁ ≤ … ≤ uₘ. A knot span is the interval between two consecutive knots, written [u<sub>i</sub>, u<sub>i+1</sub>). The order is k = p + 1. A cubic curve has p = 3 and order 4.

blocks.where: C(t) is the point at parameter t; N<sub>i,p</sub>(t) is the degree-p basis for control point i; P<sub>i</sub> is control point i; n+1 is the number of control points.

blocks.text: Counting rule: number of knots = number of control points + p + 1. In indices, m = n + p + 1, because U has m+1 entries and there are n+1 control points.
In the figure p = 3 and U has 9 knots, so m = 8. Then 8 = n + 3 + 1, n = 4, and there are 5 control points P₀ to P₄.

Uniform knots are equally spaced. Open or clamped knots repeat the first and last knot p+1 times; the curve then starts at P₀ and ends at Pₙ. Non-uniform knots have uneven spacing and allow tighter control in chosen regions.

The basis functions are built by recursion. At degree 0, N<sub>i,0</sub>(t) = 1 when u<sub>i</sub> ≤ t < u<sub>i+1</sub>, and 0 outside; the very last span is usually taken closed at the right end. For p > 0:
N<sub>i,p</sub>(t) = ((t − u<sub>i</sub>) / (u<sub>i+p</sub> − u<sub>i</sub>)) N<sub>i,p−1</sub>(t) + ((u<sub>i+p+1</sub> − t) / (u<sub>i+p+1</sub> − u<sub>i+1</sub>)) N<sub>i+1,p−1</sub>(t)
blocks.where: N<sub>i,p</sub>(t) is the basis function; u<sub>i</sub> are knots; t is the curve parameter; a term with denominator 0 is taken as 0.

blocks.text: Take 0/0 as 0. Each N<sub>i,p</sub> is nonzero only on p+1 knot spans. This short support gives local control: moving P<sub>i</sub> changes the curve only where its basis is nonzero. A Bezier control point moves the whole curve.

At a knot of multiplicity s, the curve is C<sup>(p−s)</sup> when s ≤ p. For cubic p = 3: s = 1 gives C², s = 2 gives C¹, s = 3 gives C⁰, a corner. At an end, s = p+1 clamps the curve to the end control point.
A Bezier curve is the special case p = 3 with U = (0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1). The four knots at each end make the B-spline basis become the Bernstein basis.
A B-spline surface is a tensor product of two B-spline curves. It has a control net P<sub>i,j</sub>, degrees p in u and q in v, and knot vectors U and V.
S(u,v) = Σ<sub>i=0</sub><sup>n<sub>u</sub></sup> Σ<sub>j=0</sub><sup>n<sub>v</sub></sup> N<sub>i,p</sub>(u) N<sub>j,q</sub>(v) P<sub>i,j</sub>
blocks.where: S(u,v) is a point on the surface; N<sub>i,p</sub>(u) and N<sub>j,q</sub>(v) are basis functions; P<sub>i,j</sub> is a 3D control point in the control net; p and q are the degrees in u and v; n<sub>u</sub>+1 and n<sub>v</sub>+1 are the numbers of control points in the u and v directions.

blocks.text: Continuity in u follows the same multiplicity rule; in v use q. Surfaces are used for car bodies, aircraft skins and character models.

CAD software often stores them as NURBS: Non-Uniform Rational B-Spline. A NURBS adds a weight w<sub>i</sub> to each control point and divides by the weighted sum. This lets one curve represent circles and free-form shapes exactly. We stop at that one line.

figure.caption: The nine knots of U = (0,0,0,0,1,2,2,2,2) for p = 3. The four 0s and four 2s clamp the curve to P₀ and P₄, the single 1 is an interior join with C² continuity, and 9 knots = 5 + 3 + 1 gives five control points, P₀ to P₄.

spec.aria: A row of nine knot boxes u0 to u8 holding 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, bracketed as clamped start, single interior knot with C² continuity and clamped end; below, the counting rule giving 5 control points P0 to P4 and a parameter line with 4, 1 and 4 stacked dots at u = 0, 1 and 2.

examples.question: For a cubic B-spline with p = 3 and knot vector U = (0,0,0,0,1,2,2,2,2), find the number of control points and the continuity at each knot. State whether the ends are clamped.
steps: Degree p = 3. U has 9 entries, so highest index m = 8.
Counting rule: m = n + p + 1. So 8 = n + 3 + 1 = n + 4, giving n = 4.
Number of control points is n + 1 = 5, named P₀ to P₄.
Multiplicities: 0 appears 4 times, 1 appears once, 2 appears 4 times.
At u = 0, s = 4 = p+1, so the start is clamped and the curve begins at P₀.
At u = 1, s = 1 ≤ p, so continuity is C<sup>(3−1)</sup> = C².
At u = 2, s = 4 = p+1, so the end is clamped and the curve ends at P₄. It is an end knot, not an interior join.
examples.answer: 5 control points; C² at the interior knot u = 1; both ends u = 0 and u = 2 are clamped.
examples.check:
U = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2]
p = 3
m = len(U) - 1
n = m - p - 1
cp = n + 1
c0 = U.count(0)
c1 = U.count(1)
c2 = U.count(2)
cont1 = p - c1
print(p)
print(m)
print(n)
print(cp)
print(c0)
print(c1)
print(c2)
print(cont1)

traps: Degree p and order k are not the same: k = p + 1.
The knot count is not the control point count. For n+1 control points and degree p, the knot vector has n+p+2 entries, i.e. control points + p + 1.
A B-spline does not pass through all control points. Only clamped end points are interpolated; the rest pull the curve.
At a knot of multiplicity s, continuity is C^(p−s), not C^s. For cubic, s = 3 gives C⁰, not C³.
A Bezier curve is a clamped B-spline with end multiplicity p+1, not a uniform B-spline.

quiz.q: How many knots are needed for n+1 control points of degree p?
quiz.a: n+p+2 knots, which is control points + p + 1.

quiz.q: Why does moving one B-spline control point change only a small part of the curve?
quiz.a: Each basis N_i,p is nonzero only on p+1 knot spans, so P_i has local support.

quiz.q: A cubic B-spline has U = (0,0,0,0,1,2,2,2,2). Find the number of control points.
quiz.a: m = 8; 8 = n + 3 + 1 so n = 4; control points = n+1 = 5.

quiz.q: A cubic B-spline has an interior knot of multiplicity 2, and another interior knot of multiplicity 3. Compare their continuity.
quiz.a: s = 2 gives C^(3−2) = C¹; s = 3 gives C^(3−3) = C⁰, a corner.

quiz.q: Write the knot vector that makes a cubic B-spline a Bezier curve.
What does a clamped end mean?
quiz.a: The first or last knot is repeated p+1 times, so the curve starts or ends exactly at the end control point.

beyond: Not for the exam. In industry, B-splines usually appear as NURBS inside CAD kernels and font formats; rational weights let one model exact circles, cylinders and free-form panels together. Animation and game tools use B-spline or NURBS curves as motion paths and camera rails. Newer curricula connect them to subdivision surfaces, which give smoother meshes from polygon cages. Search for NURBS basis functions, clamped knot vector, B-spline tensor product surface and de Boor algorithm.
